extra.message: Affected versions of io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded and io.netty:netty-codec-http2 are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Netty's HTTP/2 implementation fails to correctly track active streams when sending RST_STREAM in response to certain malformed control frames. An attacker can send, for example, WINDOW_UPDATE frames with a zero or overflow increment, HEADERS/DATA on a half-closed stream, or PRIORITY frames with invalid length to trigger RST_STREAMs; each reset decrements Netty's concurrent-stream counter even though the request is still processed. By repeating this on a single connection, the attacker can open an unbounded number of streams, exhausting CPU and memory and causing a denial of service.

extra.message: Affected versions of io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded and io.netty:netty-codec-http2 are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Netty's HTTP/2 implementation fails to correctly track active streams when sending RST_STREAM in response to certain malformed control frames. An attacker can send, for example, WINDOW_UPDATE frames with a zero or overflow increment, HEADERS/DATA on a half-closed stream, or PRIORITY frames with invalid length to trigger RST_STREAMs; each reset decrements Netty's concurrent-stream counter even though the request is still processed. By repeating this on a single connection, the attacker can open an unbounded number of streams, exhausting CPU and memory and causing a denial of service. This is a protocol level attack.

extra.message: Affected versions of io.netty:netty-codec-http are vulnerable to Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling'). Netty's HTTP chunked‐encoding parser treats a lone LF in a chunk extension as the end of the size line (instead of requiring CRLF per RFC 9112). If a front‐end proxy instead treats that LF as part of the extension, an attacker can craft a "funky chunks" payload that the proxy sees as one request but Netty splits into two, enabling standard HTTP request‐smuggling attacks—bypassing access controls and corrupting responses to other clients.

extra.message: Affected versions of io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded and io.netty:netty-codec-http2 are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Netty's HTTP/2 implementation fails to correctly track active streams when sending RST_STREAM in response to certain malformed control frames. An attacker can send, for example, WINDOW_UPDATE frames with a zero or overflow increment, HEADERS/DATA on a half-closed stream, or PRIORITY frames with invalid length to trigger RST_STREAMs; each reset decrements Netty's concurrent-stream counter even though the request is still processed. By repeating this on a single connection, the attacker can open an unbounded number of streams, exhausting CPU and memory and causing a denial of service.

extra.message: Affected versions of com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core and tools.jackson.core:jackson-core are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Jackson Core's non-blocking (async) JSON parser bypasses `StreamReadConstraints.maxNumberLength`, allowing an attacker to submit JSON containing extremely long numeric literals that the async parser will accept and buffer without length validation. This can trigger excessive memory allocation in the parser's `TextBuffer` and potentially severe CPU exhaustion during numeric coercion (e.g., `BigInteger`/`BigDecimal` parsing), resulting in a Denial of Service in applications using the async parser APIs (such as reactive/WebFlux pipelines).

extra.message: Affected versions of org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core are vulnerable to Improper Privilege Management. An enabled-by-default AJP Connector in Apache Tomcat treats incoming AJP requests as fully trusted and—if accessible to untrusted users—allows arbitrary files from the web application to be served or processed as JSPs. When combined with file-upload functionality (or any way for an attacker to place files into the webapp), this leads to remote code execution.

extra.message: Affected versions of io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded and io.netty:netty-codec-http2 are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Netty's HTTP/2 implementation fails to correctly track active streams when sending RST_STREAM in response to certain malformed control frames. An attacker can send, for example, WINDOW_UPDATE frames with a zero or overflow increment, HEADERS/DATA on a half-closed stream, or PRIORITY frames with invalid length to trigger RST_STREAMs; each reset decrements Netty's concurrent-stream counter even though the request is still processed. By repeating this on a single connection, the attacker can open an unbounded number of streams, exhausting CPU and memory and causing a denial of service.

extra.message: Affected versions of io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded and io.netty:netty-codec-http2 are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Netty's HTTP/2 implementation fails to correctly track active streams when sending RST_STREAM in response to certain malformed control frames. An attacker can send, for example, WINDOW_UPDATE frames with a zero or overflow increment, HEADERS/DATA on a half-closed stream, or PRIORITY frames with invalid length to trigger RST_STREAMs; each reset decrements Netty's concurrent-stream counter even though the request is still processed. By repeating this on a single connection, the attacker can open an unbounded number of streams, exhausting CPU and memory and causing a denial of service.

extra.message: The application is using an XML parser that has not been safely configured. This might lead to XML External Entity (XXE) vulnerabilities when parsing user-controlled input. An attacker can include document type definitions (DTDs) which can interact with internal or external hosts. XXE can lead to other vulnerabilities, such as Local File Inclusion (LFI), Remote Code Execution (RCE), and Server- side request forgery (SSRF), depending on the application configuration. An attacker can also use DTDs to expand recursively, leading to a Denial-of-Service (DoS) attack, also known as a Billion Laughs Attack. It is our recommendation to secure this parser against XXE attacks through parameter entities by configuring $FACTORY with `xr.setFeature(http://apache.org/xml/features/disallow- doctype-decl, true)`. Alternatively, the following configurations also provide protection against XXE attacks. `xr.setProperty(XMLConstants.ACCESS_EXTERNAL_DTD, "")` `xr.setFeature("http:// xml.org/sax/features/external-parameter-entities", false)`. For more information, see: [Java XXE prevention](https://semgrep.dev/docs/cheat-sheets/java-xxe/)

extra.message: Affected versions of io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded and io.netty:netty-codec-http2 are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Netty's HTTP/2 implementation fails to correctly track active streams when sending RST_STREAM in response to certain malformed control frames. An attacker can send, for example, WINDOW_UPDATE frames with a zero or overflow increment, HEADERS/DATA on a half-closed stream, or PRIORITY frames with invalid length to trigger RST_STREAMs; each reset decrements Netty's concurrent-stream counter even though the request is still processed. By repeating this on a single connection, the attacker can open an unbounded number of streams, exhausting CPU and memory and causing a denial of service.

extra.message: Affected versions of io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded and io.netty:netty-codec-http2 are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Netty's HTTP/2 implementation fails to correctly track active streams when sending RST_STREAM in response to certain malformed control frames. An attacker can send, for example, WINDOW_UPDATE frames with a zero or overflow increment, HEADERS/DATA on a half-closed stream, or PRIORITY frames with invalid length to trigger RST_STREAMs; each reset decrements Netty's concurrent-stream counter even though the request is still processed. By repeating this on a single connection, the attacker can open an unbounded number of streams, exhausting CPU and memory and causing a denial of service.

extra.message: Affected versions of com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core and tools.jackson.core:jackson-core are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Jackson Core's non-blocking (async) JSON parser bypasses `StreamReadConstraints.maxNumberLength`, allowing an attacker to submit JSON containing extremely long numeric literals that the async parser will accept and buffer without length validation. This can trigger excessive memory allocation in the parser's `TextBuffer` and potentially severe CPU exhaustion during numeric coercion (e.g., `BigInteger`/`BigDecimal` parsing), resulting in a Denial of Service in applications using the async parser APIs (such as reactive/WebFlux pipelines).

extra.message: Affected versions of io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded and io.netty:netty-codec-http2 are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Netty's HTTP/2 implementation fails to correctly track active streams when sending RST_STREAM in response to certain malformed control frames. extra.message: Affected versions of io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded and io.netty:netty-codec-http2 are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Netty's HTTP/2 implementation fails to correctly track active streams when sending RST_STREAM in response to certain malformed control frames. An attacker can send, for example, WINDOW_UPDATE frames with a zero or overflow increment, HEADERS/DATA on a half-closed stream, or PRIORITY frames with invalid length to trigger RST_STREAMs; each reset decrements Netty's concurrent-stream counter even though the request is still processed. By repeating this on a single connection, the attacker can open an unbounded number of streams, exhausting CPU and memory and causing a denial of service. This is a protocol level attack.

extra.message: Affected versions of org.msgpack:msgpack-core are vulnerable to Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value / Uncontrolled Resource Consumption. A denial-of-service vulnerability exists in MessagePack for Java's MessageUnpacker.readPayload()/unpackValue() and ExtensionValue.getData(): when deserializing EXT32 extension types the library lazily reads only the header but later trusts the declared 32-bit payload length and allocates a byte array of that size with no upper bound. extra.message: Affected versions of com.fasterxml.jackson.core:jackson-core and tools.jackson.core:jackson-core are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Jackson Core's non-blocking (async) JSON parser bypasses `StreamReadConstraints.maxNumberLength`, allowing an attacker to submit JSON containing extremely long numeric literals that the async parser will accept and buffer without length validation. This can trigger excessive memory allocation in the parser's `TextBuffer` and potentially severe CPU exhaustion during numeric coercion (e.g., `BigInteger`/`BigDecimal` parsing), resulting in a Denial of Service in applications using the async parser APIs (such as reactive/WebFlux pipelines).

extra.message: Affected versions of io.grpc:grpc-netty-shaded and io.netty:netty-codec-http2 are vulnerable to Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling. Netty's HTTP/2 implementation fails to correctly track active streams when sending RST_STREAM in response to certain malformed control frames. An attacker can send, for example, WINDOW_UPDATE frames with a zero or overflow increment, HEADERS/DATA on a half-closed stream, or PRIORITY frames with invalid length to trigger RST_STREAMs; each reset decrements Netty's concurrent-stream counter even though the request is still processed. By repeating this on a single connection, the attacker can open an unbounded number of streams, exhausting CPU and memory and causing a denial of service.

extra.message: Affected versions of io.netty:netty-codec-http are vulnerable to Inconsistent Interpretation of HTTP Requests ('HTTP Request/Response Smuggling'). Netty's HTTP chunked‐encoding parser treats a lone LF in a chunk extension as the end of the size line (instead of requiring CRLF per RFC 9112). extra.message: Affected versions of @angular/compiler are vulnerable to Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting'). extra.message: Affected versions of @angular/compiler are vulnerable to Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting'). A stored XSS vulnerability in the Angular Template Compiler arises because its internal security schema doesn't classify certain URL‐ holding attributes (e.g. xlink:href, math|href, annotation|href) or the `attributeName` binding on SVG animation elements (`<animate>`, `<set>`, etc.) as requiring strict URL sanitization. An attacker who can supply untrusted input to template bindings like `[attr.xlink:href]` or `<animate [attributeName]="'href'" [values]="maliciousURL">` can inject a `javascript:` URL payload. When the element is activated (e.g. clicked) or the animation runs, the malicious script executes in the application's origin, enabling session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions.

extra.message: Affected versions of @angular/compiler are vulnerable to Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting'). A stored XSS vulnerability in the Angular Template Compiler arises because its internal security schema doesn't classify certain URL‐ holding attributes (e.g. xlink:href, math|href, annotation|href) or the `attributeName` binding on SVG animation elements (`<animate>`, `<set>`, etc.) as requiring strict URL sanitization. An attacker who can supply untrusted input to template bindings like `[attr.xlink:href]` or `<animate [attributeName]="'href'" [values]="maliciousURL">` can inject a `javascript:` URL payload. When the element is activated (e.g. clicked) or the animation runs, the malicious script executes in the application's origin, enabling session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions.

An attacker who can supply untrusted input to template bindings like `[attr.xlink:href]` or `<animate [attributeName]="'href'" [values]="maliciousURL">` can inject a `javascript:` URL payload. When the element is activated (e.g. clicked) or the animation runs, the malicious script executes in the application's origin, enabling session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions.

Angular's template compiler fails to classify the `href` and `xlink:href` attributes on SVG `<script>` elements as Resource URL contexts. A stored XSS vulnerability in the Angular Template Compiler arises because its internal security schema doesn't classify certain URL‐ holding attributes (e.g. xlink:href, math|href, annotation|href) or the `attributeName` binding on SVG animation elements (`<animate>`, `<set>`, etc.) as requiring strict URL sanitization. An attacker who can supply untrusted input to template bindings like `[attr.xlink:href]` or `<animate [attributeName]="'href'" [values]="maliciousURL">` can inject a `javascript:` URL payload. When the element is activated (e.g. clicked) or the animation runs, the malicious script executes in the application's origin, enabling session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions.

extra.message: Affected versions of @angular/compiler are vulnerable to Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting'). A stored XSS vulnerability in the Angular Template Compiler arises because its internal security schema doesn't classify certain URL‐ holding attributes (e.g. xlink:href, math|href, annotation|href) or the `attributeName` binding on SVG animation elements (`<animate>`, `<set>`, etc.) as requiring strict URL sanitization. An attacker who can supply untrusted input to template bindings like `[attr.xlink:href]` or `<animate [attributeName]="'href'" [values]="maliciousURL">` can inject a `javascript:` URL payload. When the element is activated (e.g. clicked) or the animation runs, the malicious script executes in the application's origin, enabling session hijacking, data exfiltration, or unauthorized actions.
